requirements:
# Recipe Management System - **Difficulty:** Hard (hard) ## Requirements A factory's production line needs to produce a variety of products based on different recipes. The control center of the production line requires a recipe management system that allows operators to add, delete, modify, and query recipe data. Control requirements: Recipe data should include recipe number, raw material type, raw material ratio, and production temperature. The system should allow input of new recipe data and store it in the recipe database. The system should allow deletion or modification of existing recipe data by recipe number. The system should allow querying recipe details by recipe number and output the recipe. Notes: 1. Recipes are constructed using the ST_Recipe data type, which includes recipe number (recipeID), raw material type (ingredientType), raw material ratio (ingredientRatio), and production temperature (productionTemperature). The recipe database can store up to 10 recipes, constructed with ARRAY[1..10] OF ST_Recipe, where recipe numbers must not be duplicated, and a recipe number of 0 indicates an empty slot. 2. When a query recipe request signal (queryRecipe) is triggered, the system first compares the recipe number (recipeID) from the input recipe (recipeIn) with all recipes in the recipe database recipe. If the number does not exist, an error status (error=true) and error code (status=16#8001) are output. If the number exists, the recipe is output to the recipe query result (recipeQueryResult). 3. When an add recipe request signal (addRecipe) is triggered, the system first compares the recipe number (recipeID) from the input recipe (recipeIn) with all recipes in the recipe database (recipe). If a duplicate number exists, an error status (error=true) and error code (status=16#8002) are output. If there is no empty slot in the recipe database (recipe), an error status (error=true) and error code (status=16#8003) are output. If there are no errors, the input recipe (recipeIn) is stored in the recipe database (recipe), prioritizing the empty slot with the smallest array index. 4. When a delete recipe request signal (deleteRecipe) is triggered, the system first compares the recipe number (recipeID) from the input recipe (recipeIn) with all recipes in the recipe database (recipe). If the number does not exist, an error status (error=true) and error code (status=16#8004) are output. If the number exists, the recipe is deleted, i.e., the recipe number (recipeID) in the recipe database (recipe) is set to 0. 5. When a modify recipe request signal (modifyRecipe) is triggered, the system first compares the recipe number (recipeID) from the input recipe (recipeIn) with all recipes in the recipe database (recipe). If the number does not exist, an error status (error=true) and error code (status=16#8005) are output. If the number exists, the recipe is replaced with the input recipe (recipeIn). ## Interface Definition | Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Input | `addRecipe` | `BOOL` | Add Recipe Request Signal | | Input | `deleteRecipe` | `BOOL` | Delete Recipe Request Signal | | Input | `modifyRecipe` | `BOOL` | Modify Recipe Request Signal | | Input | `queryRecipe` | `BOOL` | Query Recipe Request Signal | | Input | `recipeIn` | `ST_Recipe` | Input Recipe | | Output | `recipeAdded` | `BOOL` | Recipe Added Success Indicator | | Output | `recipeDeleted` | `BOOL` | Recipe Deleted Success Indicator | | Output | `recipeModified` | `BOOL` | Recipe Modified Success Indicator | | Output | `recipeQueryResult` | `ST_Recipe` | Recipe Query Result Output | | Output | `error` | `BOOL` | Error Status Indicator
FALSE: No Error Occurred
TRUE: Execution Error | | Output | `status` | `WORD` | Status Code | | Input/Output | `recipe` | `ARRAY[1..10] OF ST_Recipe` | Recipe Database | **Data type `ST_Recipe`** | Field | Data Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `recipeID` | `INT` | Recipe identifier; zero denotes an unused database slot. | | `ingredientType` | `INT` | Ingredient-type identifier. | | `ingredientRatio` | `REAL` | Ingredient proportion. | | `productionTemperature` | `REAL` | Production temperature. |

interface.name: error
interface.description:
Error Status Indicator
FALSE: No Error Occurred
TRUE: Execution Error

scan_semantics: Inputs I[k] are sampled at invocation; outputs O[k] are observed after the call. Retained pre-state q[k] becomes q[k+1]. Each test resets the instance. A transition affects the same observed scan. dt_ms is elapsed time since the preceding invocation; the first invocation starts IEC timers at elapsed zero. CycleTime inputs, where supplied, are attributed to the current invocation rather than inferred from dt_ms.
safety_priority: Failed requests must not mutate the database.
Insertion uses the lowest-index empty slot.
assumptions: At most one request rises per call. Requests use rising edges; simultaneous request priority is unspecified by the source.
Only positive nonzero IDs are submitted; zero denotes an unused slot.
Success indicators are one-invocation pulses. error/status clear on idle.
recipeQueryResult retains the last successful query until another successful query.
Deleting a record clears only its recipeID; its other fields become unconstrained.
The caller-owned recipe array is initialized once and persists across steps; do not overwrite it with initial values per scan.
Compare REAL values with absolute tolerance 1e-5.
The specification_contract is normative and supplied identically to both frameworks. Output names always denote observed candidate outputs, never precomputed expected values.

Floating-point inputs and intermediate reference arithmetic are finite. Existing fixed traces retain their declared absolute tolerance; claims do not extend to arbitrary magnitudes without a separately specified numeric error policy.

atomic_propositions.q_missing: rising(queryRecipe) AND ID absent from pre-database
atomic_propositions.a_full: rising(addRecipe) AND ID absent AND all slots full
atomic_propositions.error: O[k].error: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.
atomic_propositions.add_ok: rising(addRecipe) AND positive ID absent AND empty slot exists
atomic_propositions.insert: lowest-index pre-empty slot equals recipeIn; all other slots unchanged
atomic_propositions.add_success: recipeAdded AND NOT error AND status=0
atomic_propositions.clear: NOT error AND status=0 AND NOT recipeAdded AND NOT recipeDeleted AND NOT recipeModified
atomic_propositions.unique: all nonzero IDs are pairwise distinct
atomic_propositions.CompleteBehaviorV2:
令(Sref[k+1], E[k])=T_PUB017(Sref[k], deepCopy(I[k]), dt_ms[k])。T由normalized_specification.transition列出的固定Python源码和初始状态精确定义。CompleteBehaviorV2[k] 当且仅当所有constrained_observed_fields均存在于实际O[k]，且分别满足comparison关系。Sref只由采样输入推进，绝不由O或候选内部变量推进。
数据库首拍由调用前recipe初始化，之后为跨拍保留存储；非零ID唯一，输入ID正且每拍至多一个请求上升沿。四请求历史初值FALSE、每拍更新。查询缺失8001；新增重复8002优先于满库8003，否则最低空位整体写入；删除缺失8004否则只清ID；修改缺失8005否则整体替换。失败/空闲库保持。三个成功输出是单拍脉冲，成功/空闲error=FALSE/status=0；查询结果仅成功查询时更新，初值零记录。成功删除槽的非ID字段当拍不受约束，此后无覆盖操作时与采样实际值比较保持；不把这些物理表示字段写回参考数据库。
atomic_propositions.recipeAdded: O[k].recipeAdded: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.
atomic_propositions.recipeDeleted: O[k].recipeDeleted: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.
atomic_propositions.recipeModified: O[k].recipeModified: independently observed post-scan candidate value (BOOL); never defined as expected output.
atomic_propositions.recipeQueryResult: O[k].recipeQueryResult: independently observed post-scan candidate value (ST_Recipe); never defined as expected output.
atomic_propositions.status: O[k].status: independently observed post-scan candidate value (WORD); never defined as expected output.
atomic_propositions.recipe: O[k].recipe: independently observed post-scan candidate value (ARRAY[1..10] OF ST_Recipe); never defined as expected output. I[k].recipe denotes separately captured caller value before invocation.

ltl.name: Errors
ltl.formula: G((q_missing -> e1) & (a_dup -> e2) & (a_full -> e3) & (d_missing -> e4) & (m_missing -> e5))
ltl.explanation: Distinct failures produce the official status codes.

ltl.name: Lowest insertion
ltl.explanation: Adds use the lowest free slot.

ltl.name: Query
ltl.explanation: Query returns the complete matched record.

ltl.name: Idle
ltl.explanation: Indicators and invocation errors clear on idle.

ltl.name: Uniqueness
ltl.explanation: All operations preserve ID uniqueness from a valid initial database.

Every constrained ACTUAL output satisfies the exact pinned input-driven reference transition and comparison policy. Finite observations can falsify this predicate; no completed unbounded proof is claimed.

tests.name: CRUD
tests.purpose: Add, query, modify, delete and reuse the first empty slot.
tests.notes: Bind persistent recipe storage once. Inspect recipe[1].recipeID=2 after reuse; deleted non-ID fields are unconstrained.

tests.name: missing_duplicate
tests.purpose: All missing-record errors and duplicate rejection preserve existing record.

tests.name: capacity_priority
tests.purpose: Fill ten slots; duplicate error has priority over full error.

specification_contract.history_binding: I, O and Sref namespaces, initialization and updates are defined in normalized_specification.observation, history_bindings and reference_state_initial. Candidate output never drives Sref.
specification_contract.evaluation_scope: Versioned executable scan predicate plus LTL over interpreted predicates. No native checker encoding or completed formal proof is claimed.
specification_contract.transition_binding: Use normalized_specification.transition and exact pinned source snapshots.

normalized_specification.language: LTL over typed scan predicates; finite conjunction is a binding-time macro, not native NuSMV syntax.

transition.reference_binding: Persistent plc_agent.scan_contract.ScanContract('PUB017'); constructed once per independent case, current state is Sref[k].
transition.state_update: Exactly once per scan; mutations of sampled IN_OUT copies are reference effects, not observations.
transition.hash_encoding: UTF-8 without BOM; all line endings normalized to LF before SHA256

comparison.integer_boolean: exact type and value; no tolerance
comparison.float: finite; abs error<=1e-5; dictionary/list shape and non-float values exact
comparison.PUB008: only successfully converted channels[j].outputValue: abs<=1e-5 OR rel<=2e-6; all preserved/config fields exact
comparison.PUB017: Successful deletion constrains recipeID=0; other fields of that deleted slot are unconstrained for the deletion scan. Subsequent no-write scans preserve the sampled actual representation. This observer history is separate from the logical reference database.
comparison.TIME_LTIME: exact integer nanoseconds after IEC literal parsing
comparison.implementation: plc_agent.normalized_spec.NormalizedScanMonitor.step with output_matches (pinned sources); observer histories never drive the independent logical reference

observation.I[k]: deep-copied inputs immediately before invocation k
observation.O[k]: actual outputs immediately after invocation k, supplied by independent execution backend
observation.Sref[k]: independent reference state BEFORE k; unrelated to similarly named candidate variables
observation.initial: fresh instance BEFORE invocation 0; never substituted by O[0]
observation.X: next scan-sequence position; argument must be Boolean, not a numeric term
observation.time: dt_ms is observed elapsed time; public timers use physical time, SELF Tick/count timers use logical scans

auxiliary_state_bindings.Spre: Sref[k], before the invocation; initialized by reference_state_initial
auxiliary_state_bindings.Spost: Sref[k+1], after exactly one pinned transition on I[k]
auxiliary_state_bindings.first: k=0 (first invocation); distinct from the pre-invocation initial observation
auxiliary_state_bindings.pre-output: actual O[k-1] for OUTPUT (explicit history initial where declared); I[k] for caller-owned IN_OUT
auxiliary_state_bindings.previous-input: I[k-1] for k>=1; edge memory for BOOL requests initially FALSE and updated after EVERY invocation
auxiliary_state_bindings.reference_warning: Spre/Spost predicates are input-driven ghosts, not evidence that candidate internals match. Conclusions about the candidate must constrain actual O.

storage.pre_database: Spre.data_contract.recipes; first invocation uses separately sampled I[0].recipe
storage.capacity: length of the actual caller buffer binding, fixed per case

normalized_specification.reference_state_rule: Initial state is the serialized constructor above; all fields update solely through the pinned transition. Ghost phase/history/queue are names for this state, not observed candidate state.

primitives.bitwise: DWORD AND/NOT and popcount operate on unsigned 32-bit values; complement is masked by 0xFFFFFFFF.
primitives.time_literals: IEC TIME/LTIME literals are exact integer durations in nanoseconds.
primitives.observed_arrays: All IN_OUT inputs are snapshots before invocation; outputs are independently acquired after invocation. Physical bounds map by ordinal, never share another array lower bound.
primitives.boolean_next: X takes a Boolean formula. Numeric history transport is bit-expanded for DWORD; Boolean histories use equivalence.
primitives.time_progress: Timed eventuality clauses explicitly require G(F(TimeTick)); TimeTick denotes crossing a new integer-ms boundary. Finite observations cannot establish this premise.

Focused legacy LTL predicates still require backend lowering; normalization is not model-checker acceptance.
